command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Redfish reset concept matches, but the example posts to /Systems/system rather than the discovered action target and uses insecure TLS/secrets/fixed sleep. It also does not resolve whether PowerCycle satisfies ForceRestart.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover the exact Reset action and allowable types, use the engineer-selected type once with verified TLS/protected credentials, and prove transition plus reboot identity and recovery under bounded monitoring.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Literal ResetType PowerCycle, Criteria term ForceRestart, post-action PowerState check and 10/20-minute estimates are all preserved pending semantic resolution.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Model the action as an approved state transition with pre-state/boot ID, immutable request and response, BMC/host outage/reachability timestamps, new boot ID and final health; bind everything to the same serial/resource.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds action discovery, semantic decision, secure credentials/TLS, workload governance and bounded recovery rather than guessed URI, grep and fixed delay.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final PowerState alone cannot prove the requested reset class occurred; transition/outage and a new host boot identity are necessary, and PowerCycle cannot be assumed equivalent to ForceRestart.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Reset can interrupt workloads or leave the host unavailable. There is no safe automatic rollback or retry, and implementations may expose different reset semantics.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure explicitly sends ResetType PowerCycle, while Criteria says the SUT should be ForceRestart. These are distinct Redfish reset concepts on many implementations, and the source gives no firmware mapping or transition contract proving equivalence.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The conflict and required approval block execution/verdict, not static review; the unresolved decision is queued while library review proceeds.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 1962 Wistron-BMC-00998-V002: decide whether the authoritative reset is Procedure ResetType=PowerCycle or Criteria ForceRestart (or provide the exact firmware mapping proving equivalence), and define expected transition/outage, final PowerState, boot-identity proof and recovery deadline.

review_improvement: Separates reset class from final power state, exposes the source semantic conflict and requires one-shot causal reboot/recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A host can end in the same PowerState after different reset classes, so the post-GET cannot distinguish PowerCycle from ForceRestart. Causal evidence needs the exact accepted request, reachability transition and a changed boot identifier tied to the same physical SUT. Because a timeout may mean the first reset is still progressing, issuing another request can compound outage or corruption; therefore no automatic retry is part of correctness, not just caution.
